component.notes:
Amazon Fire TV (Fire OS models) over IP, through the Matchstick bridge service. Not supported: Fire TV models running Vega OS (Fire TV Stick 4K Select, Fire TV Stick HD 2026 and newer sticks).
KEYBOARD VERSION: the Savant Pro app's text entry and pairing pop-ups work for this Fire TV. Built like Savant's Apple TV (atv-bridge) profile, without the atv-bridge service: the Pro app's SendText, ClearText, PairStart and PairSubmitPin go to the Matchstick bridge. Pairing a Fire TV is the 'Allow USB debugging?' prompt on the TV; there is no PIN. Unpair in the app is ignored (the Fire TV stays connected). Back, Stop, Scan, Skip and Setup are custom actions. The app's TV button is Home; a quick double press does the "Double Home Action" (default: Live TV). The app shows this service as Apple TV: set Brand to Display = Amazon Fire TV and a service alias.
SETUP 1. Install the bridge on the Savant host (install.sh) and pair the Fire TV once: firetvctl pair [fire-tv-ip] 2. Set this component's IP address to the machine running the bridge (normally this Savant host). Port 2360. 3. Inspector, State Variables: set "Fire TV IP Address" to the Fire TV's IP (give it a DHCP reservation). 4. Wire the HDMI output to the display or switcher like any source.
One component per Fire TV; all of them point at the same bridge. LaunchApp takes an alias (appletv, disneyplus, hulu, kodi, max, netflix, paramountplus, peacock, plex, pluto, primevideo, settings, sling, spotify, youtube, youtubetv) or any Android package name. Volume/Mute custom actions go to the TV/AVR over HDMI-CEC; normally route volume to the AVR/TV in Savant. Gate automations on ONLINE = 1. If LAST_ERROR is not blank it says what to fix.
====================== Change Log ================== Version: 1.4 Change: Keyboard version (Pro app text entry and pairing), LiveTV action, Double Home Action, file names Blueprint can find (amazon_fire tv (...).xml). Needs Matchstick bridge 1.4. Version: 1.1 Change: Rebuilt on Savant's Roku profile structure (service generation, standard button names). Version: 1.0 Change: Initial release.

state_variable.name: Fire TV IP Address
state_variable.note: IP address of this Fire TV, e.g. 192.168.1.50

state_variable.name: ADB
state_variable.note: CONNECTED, UNAUTHORIZED (approve on TV) or OFFLINE

state_variable.name: APP_NAME
state_variable.note: Friendly name of the app on screen (Netflix, Home ...)

state_variable.name: APP_PACKAGE
state_variable.note: Android package of the app on screen

state_variable.name: LAST_ERROR
state_variable.note: Blank when healthy; otherwise what to fix

state_variable.name: KeyboardFocused
state_variable.note: true while a text box is on screen

state_variable.name: Discovered
state_variable.note: true when the Fire TV answers on the network

state_variable.name: PairingState
state_variable.note: unpaired, awaiting_pin (approve on the TV) or paired

state_variable.name: PairingError
state_variable.note: Why pairing is waiting or failed

state_variable.name: Double Home Action
state_variable.note: What a quick double press of Home (the app's TV button) does: livetv (Live TV guide), off, an app alias or package (netflix, com.hulu.plus), or key:<android keycode>

action_argument.name: PIN
action_argument.note: Ignored: approve on the TV screen

action_argument.name: AppID
action_argument.note: Package name, e.g. com.netflix.ninja, or an alias such as netflix

action_argument.name: TextMessage
action_argument.note: Text to put in the box
